newsitem.title: USA: Wallace recommends vote against Wyser-Pratte.
newsitem.headline: Wallace recommends vote against Wyser-Pratte.

text.p: Wallace Computer Services Inc said Thursday its directors will unanimously recommend that shareholders at its annual meeting vote against proposals by Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc.
Wyser-Pratte holds 2.3 percent of Wallace Computer Services' outstanding shares and has proposed three candidates as directors of the computer services company.

"The board of directors of Wallace Computer Services has met and carefully reviewed your purported notice and annual meeting proposals," according to a letter being sent from Wallace Computer Services directors to Wyser-Pratte.

"After considering the merits of your actions, the board has unanimously concluded that neither the election of your purported nominees nor the adoption of your proposals would be in the best interests of Wallace or the shareholders, and, accordingly, the Wallace board will unanimously recommend that the shareholders vote for the Wallace board's director nominees and vote against your proposals," the letter said.
Wallace Computer Services said it is aware that Wyser-Pratte tried to contact the three Wallace directors who were nominated by Moore Corp Ltd at last year's annual meeting.
In early August, Moore, a huge Canadian business forms manufacturer, abandoned a 13-month campaign to acquire Wallace Computer Services in a $1.3 billion deal.
"Your phone calls to them as well as your preliminary proxy statement suggest that you believe that these three directors are predisposed to supporting your attempted proxy contest," the letter said.

"You should be under no illusion that you or your purported director nominees have three allies on the Wallace board. We want to emphasize that we are unanimous in opposing your actions," the letter said.
In mid-August, Wyser-Pratte filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission proposals it wanted included in Wallace Computer Services' proxy for its November 6 annual meeting.

In addition to the three directors, Wyser-Pratte proposed creation of a special committee to explore ways to maximize shareholder value. It also seeks repeal of a company bylaw which requires an 80 percent vote to approve certain mergers.

Yesterday Wallace Computer Services reported fiscal fourth quarter and full-year earnings that it said exceeded analysts' expectations and company forecasts. At the same time, Wallace Computer Services raised its quarterly dividend.
Guy Wyser-Pratte, president of Wyser-Pratte, said on Thursday that he would continue to push his proposals. He declined to elaborate.
He said that although Wallace Computer Services had increased its dividend substantially and reported higher than expected earnings, the stock was only up 1/8 to 27-1/8.
"They're not delivering value to sharehodlers," he said. "The stock's up an eighth with all that happening."
Factoring in the company's stock split, the stock is trading at just over 54, compared to Moore's offer last year of $60, he said.
"A year ago Wallace could have had at least $60 per share from Moore," he said. "The stock now is trading on a pro forma basis at 54."
"It's been a year and nothing has happened with the stock," he said.
